answer: One concrete defense is a refundable entry bond that vests slowly. Each new agent locks a deposit before it can earn, and rewards drip out over many epochs. Spinning up an ocean of clones means locking a bond for every one, while graders view each through a prism of timing, wording and funding overlap; matched clusters forfeit their bonds. Honest agents reach an oasis of liquidity once vesting ends, but a sybil farm pays N deposits upfront and risks all of them, so the attack costs more than it earns.
